name: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 5

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for SCA5

criteria.description: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with gait and limb incoordination
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Pathogenic mutation in the SPTBN2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
MRI evidence of cerebellar atrophy without significant brainstem involvement
Exclusion of other causes of ataxia such as acquired or metabolic etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive cerebellar ataxia, positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance, and identification of a pathogenic SPTBN2 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may overlap with other SCAs.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of metabolic causes of ataxia
imaging: MRI showing cerebellar cortical atrophy predominantly affecting the vermis and hemispheres
other: Electromyography may show mild peripheral neuropathy
Neurophysiological studies typically normal or mildly abnormal

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pyramidal signs and extrapyramidal symptoms
Earlier onset in childhood or adolescence
Presence of cardiomyopathy and diabetes mellitus
GAA trinucleotide repeat expansion in FXN gene

redFlags: Rapid progression of ataxia over months
Presence of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
Onset before age 10 or after age 70
references: Klockgether T. Spinocerebellar ataxia. Handb Clin Neurol. 2018;147:233-247.
Synofzik M, Schüle R. Spinocerebellar ataxias: clinical features, genetics, and pathogenesis. Handb Clin Neurol. 2018;155:233-255.
